govdocs-archive_org-nsia-BishopJim_Bisho: This Jim Bishop profile — creator unknown — is a piece on the journalist. Bishop wrote The Day Lincoln Was Shot. His books sold millions. The file belongs to the press archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-CIAJim_CIA_Jim: This UPI report — ‘Jim,’ former CIA contract agent, claims CIA role — covers an ex-agent’s claims. The wire story belongs to the intelligence archive. Such claims should be read critically. Wire copy moved fast. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-HoughtonJim_Hou: Harold Weisberg’s letter to Tony Marro of Newsday on Jim Hougan’s Secret Agenda is a researcher’s note. Weisberg sparred with fellow authors. The letter is sharp. The file belongs to the press archive. The item is a fragment of correspondence.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-McNicholasJim_M: This item — McNicholas, Jim — is a National Security Internet Archive file. The file’s full context is unclear. Its subject seems to be the JFK case. The file may hold a clue. Archivists value such fragments. The item is a fragment of the archive.
george-leatrim: Susanna Moodie, famous for her memoir Roughing It in the Bush, sets this tale in the Canada she knew as a settler. Young George Leatrim faces the hardships and temptations of pioneer life in a story meant to guide as well as entertain. Moodie's clear-eyed view of the backwoods gives the narrative an honest, lived-in feel.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abarim: This 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia article on Abarim — the mountain range in Moab where Moses viewed the Promised Land — covers its geography and scripture. Anthony Maas maps the biblical references. A handy reference on a storied landscape. Nebo's summit, where Moses died gazing westward, crowns the range.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-albert-von-be: This 1913 reference piece on Albert von Behaim — the papal legate who defied Frederick II. Francis Schaefer tells his bold stand. He carried the pope's thunder to Germany. Princes trembled at his interdicts. A legate who feared no emperor. His letters reveal the curia's mind.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-anton-joseph-: A 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia entry on Anton Joseph Binterim — the German liturgist. William Devlin honors his Denkwürdigkeiten. His volumes mapped the Church's rites. The parish priest became the scholars' guide. A pastor among the antiquaries. His feast days fill the German calendars.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-arnold-pannar: A 1913 entry on Pannartz and Sweinheim — the first printers of Italy. Klemens Löffler honors their Subiaco press. Their Latin classics founded the trade. Rome's presses descend from theirs. The fathers of the Italian book. Their Bible was the press's crown.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-baal-baalim: A 1913 entry on Baal and Baalim — the Canaanite gods of the Old Testament. Charles Souvay tells their dark worship. The prophets thundered against their altars. Jezebel brought their cult to Israel. The idols of the ancient Levant. Their groves crowned the high places.
